headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.52–1.04), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin B6 and renal cell carcinoma. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 81.52%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

sample_size.excerpt: This analysis included 455 RCC cases and 455 matched controls with complete data on all markers and covariates. A comparison of the included 910 participants vs 194 excluded with missing data is shown in Table S1 .

effect_size.excerpt: The association between PLP and RCC risk was similar across the three models with an OR (90% CrI) for a 1 SD increase in log PLP of 0.72 (0.64, 0.82), 0.75 (0.66, 0.86) and 0.76 (0.66, 0.87) from the minimally adjusted, BMI and smoking adjusted, and mutually adjusted models, respectively (Table 3 ).

comparison.excerpt: All regression model results for continuous predictors are presented per 1 SD increase.

timing.excerpt: Because this case‐control study was nested within the EPIC cohort, plasma samples were collected at baseline in all participants, with data available for cases often years prior to their diagnosis.
